clue.text: Stone needs fix to get around being loaded

definitions.note: the jet set are wealthy people who travel the world, so the phrase describes them rather than defining them strictly

parts.note: jet is a black stone used in jewellery
to set is to fix firmly

explanation.surface: A druggy Rolling Stone craves a hit to be able to go out, or so it reads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' and 'fix' suggest drugs; they are a gemstone and the verb set. 'Loaded' means rich.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are rich, fashionable people who fly from one resort to another, i.e. travelling while wealthy.

clue.text: About flies Bardot's undone and various creative works'

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes round the other word
undone means unravelled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Brigitte Bardot, the French film star
jets fly, so flies here is a plural noun

explanation.surface: Brigitte Bardot's trouser flies come undone, as do her various artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like the opening of trousers but is the plural noun for aircraft. 'undone' rearranges the actress's name to OBDART, and 'About' puts that round the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Objets d'art are small decorative or artistic pieces collected for their beauty, a French phrase for art objects.

clue.text: Medicine makes great organ subside, getting small

parts.note: a nod to the setter's name: a Cyclops has one great eye
to subside is to drop or sink
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A drug is said to make a big member go down, which the readers will enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great organ' suggests something rude; it is an eye, fitting Cyclops's single giant eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye drops are a liquid treatment dripped into the eyes, a form of medication.

clue.text: Spots rising politician make a pitch

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read upwards, i.e. in reverse

parts.note: acne is spots on the skin
MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A spotty young politician makes a sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up camp, i.e. pitch tents; 'pitch' looks like a sales talk.

clue.text: Red-nose star, bog standard at first, being without a speciality

indicators.note: this piece comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: bog is British slang for a lavatory, and WC (water closet) is its standard term
fields are areas of expertise; the clue gestures at these without a neat synonym, a loose reading

explanation.surface: A clown with a red nose is called ordinary and without any special talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' puts WC at the front; the FIELDS part is only loosely clued, as fields are specialist areas.
explanation.definitionFit: W.C. Fields, the American comic actor, was famous for his bulbous red drinker's nose.

clue.text: Trick document is fair means of getting plenty of bangs

definitions.text: fair means of getting plenty of bangs

parts.note: a dodge is a trick or scheme
a document is a manuscript, MS; only its M is used here, a loose touch the clue does not signal

explanation.surface: A con on paper is presented as an honest route to lots of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' means a funfair, not honest, and 'bangs' are collisions, not sex. The manuscript abbreviation MS supplies only its M.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgem is a bumper car at a funfair, driven to crash repeatedly into others.

clue.text: Leamington's legless, weight-shedding, dead awful leader

indicators.note: losing a ton, a unit of weight, along with the G left over from leg
without leg: its L and E come off the front of the town's name, and its G goes at the next step

parts.note: Leamington Spa, a town in Warwickshire; that the answer also sits inside the name is a coincidence, as the clue works by removal

explanation.surface: A drunk, slimming man from Leamington is a terrible boss, now dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legless' (British slang for very drunk) removes LEG: LE from the front gives AMINGTON, and the G goes with TON when 'weight-shedding' removes it, leaving AMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Idi Amin was the brutal dictator of Uganda in the 1970s, who died in 2003.

clue.text: Habits formed by drug suppliers replacing tranquillizers initially with Ecstasy

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: chemists dispense medicines

indicators.note: only the first letter is used

parts.note: its first letter is T
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Addictions are created by dealers who swap sedatives for ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T from tranquillizers, and 'replacing' swaps that T in CHEMISTS for E. 'Habits' suggests addictions; here it means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit can be a garment, as in a nun's or riding habit; a chemise is a loose dress or shift.

clue.text: At an early stage, Cyclops goes arse over tip — like the poet, needs internal adjustment

indicators.note: turning head over heels flips the word end to end, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: the setter, Cyclops, speaking of himself, is ME

indicators.note: the letters inside the word are shuffled, so it calls for a rearrangement

parts.note: Byronic means in the manner of the poet Lord Byron

explanation.surface: The setter tumbles over, hoping to look poetic, in a crude bit of self-mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes arse over tip' turns ME into EM; 'needs internal adjustment' rearranges BYRONIC to BRYONIC by swapping its inner letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something embryonic is undeveloped, still at its beginning, as an embryo is the first stage of life.

clue.text: Balls + speed = sex-appeal

parts.note: two balls drawn as round letters, O and O
MPH, miles per hour, is the unit of speed

explanation.surface: A crude equation: testicles plus velocity add up to allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour or sexual attractiveness, the quality that draws attention.

clue.text: Shift going out of fashion means finding a potential shag quickly?

parts.note: to shift is to move fast, to speed
something becoming old-fashioned is dating

explanation.surface: A change in style seems to be offered as a way to find a quick fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shag' is British slang for sex. The question mark marks a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed dating rotates singles through brief meetings, a rapid way of finding a possible partner.

clue.text: Monica reportedly getting end away — avoided by Clinton

indicators.note: the last letter is taken off; the phrase is also British slang for having sex

parts.note: Monica said aloud is moniker, and a moniker is a name

explanation.surface: Gossip about Monica Lewinsky's affair, which Bill Clinton denied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting end away' drops the last letter of NAME, and is also British slang for sex, matching the Lewinsky story. NAM is short for Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton famously escaped the draft for the Vietnam War, often called 'Nam.

clue.text: Votes Conservative, hiding provisional concern

indicators.note: the answer is concealed within the run of letters of the clue's first two words

parts.note: the letters run on through voTES COnservative

explanation.surface: A voter backs the Tories while keeping a provisional worry to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' signals the answer concealed across voTES COnservative. 'provisional' looks political but means 'selling provisions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tesco is Britain's biggest supermarket chain, a business (concern) that sells provisions, i.e. groceries.

clue.text: Amis loses head in e-plots fiasco — "they produce controversial reading"

indicators.note: the shortened name is placed inside the rearranged letters
a fiasco is a mess, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Martin Amis, the novelist, whose name loses its opening A

explanation.surface: Martin Amis is humiliated in some online scheme gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' cuts AMIS to MIS, which goes 'in' POLETS, the anagram from 'fiasco'.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemists write polemics, forceful attacks on an opinion, which make contentious reading.

clue.text: Campbell's job: providing great copy

parts.note: super means great
a model is a copy or replica

explanation.surface: Alastair Campbell, Blair's spin doctor, is praised for producing good press material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Campbell' suggests Alastair Campbell, Tony Blair's press chief; it is Naomi Campbell.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi Campbell is a famous British supermodel, so being a top fashion model is her career.

clue.text: Standard celeb on beach hiding end of his bollocks

indicators.note: one piece comes next to the other, in the order of the clue

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

indicators.note: the outer word contains what follows

parts.note: a beach is sands

indicators.note: the last letter is the one taken

parts.note: its final letter is S
British slang for nonsense, i.e. tripe

explanation.surface: A tabloid picture of a famous man on a beach, his privates on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes S from 'his'; SANDS is 'hiding' S plus TRIPE, giving SANDSTRIPES, and STAR goes 'on' the front. 'Bollocks' means nonsense here.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and the Stars and Stripes is the national flag of the United States.

clue.text: Be an MP (pissed) and refuse to go!

parts.note: an MP sits for a constituency
British slang for drunk, as is tight

explanation.surface: A drunken Member of Parliament won't leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit tight is to stay put and wait rather than moving, i.e. stubbornly staying.

clue.text: Is pettily critical of grooms, in a beastly way

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to nitpick is to find fault over trivial details
second meaning: monkeys groom each other by picking out nits

explanation.walkthrough: 'grooms' looks like bridegrooms being criticised; it is the verb, as animals clean one another.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both fussy fault-finding and the literal act of removing lice eggs from fur.

clue.text: Queer version of Abba's for afters?

parts.note: rum and queer both mean odd

indicators.note: a new version reorders the letters

parts.note: ABBA, the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A gay cover of an ABBA song is offered as dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges ABBAS to BABAS. 'Queer' means strange here, and 'afters' is British slang for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum babas are small yeast cakes soaked in rum syrup, served as a pudding at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Bristol garrison, a model of reciprocal action

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: Bristol City rhymes with titty, so a Bristol is a breast, a tit
a garrison is a fort
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A soldier's posting in Bristol is held up as an example of give and take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bristols' is rhyming slang for breasts, so one Bristol is a TIT; 'Bristol' looks like the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is retaliation in kind, an equivalent response for each blow, i.e. a reciprocal exchange.

clue.text: Pisspoor royal, holding line, gets in the way of head

indicators.note: something piss-poor is badly made, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A useless royal obstructs the head of something, perhaps a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: ROYAL holding L gives the letters RLOYAL, which 'Pisspoor' shuffles. 'Giving head' is slang for oral sex, so 'in the way of head' means orally.
explanation.definitionFit: Orally means by mouth, which is the manner in which oral sex is performed.

clue.text: Hard working type has jar — not pissed, though

indicators.note: pissed means drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grafter has a drink but stays sober.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says 'not pissed', but 'pissed' is the anagram signal working on JAR and NOT together.
explanation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan means to work tirelessly, so a Trojan is a person of great energy and industry.

clue.text: Expression of gay person: 'male circumference not good'

indicators.note: the following word is the part left out

parts.note: a girth is a measurement round something

explanation.surface: A camp quip about a man whose measurements disappoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' good removes G from GIRTH, leaving IRTH. 'gay' is in its old sense of cheerful, though the surface suggests the modern one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth is laughter and merriment, how a cheerful (gay, in the older sense) person shows their happiness.

clue.text: City male holding skirt up

indicators.note: the first word contains the second

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read in reverse

parts.note: a rara is a short flounced skirt, popular in the 1980s

explanation.surface: A man in the city lifts a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RARA into ARAR, and HE is 'holding' it. 'skirt' looks like slang for women; it is a rara skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital and largest city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Tube users' conception curtailed

parts.note: test-tube babies are conceived by in vitro fertilisation, and the name is cut down to its initials

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground; here it is a test tube. 'Curtailed' means the phrase in vitro fertilisation is shortened to its initials, so there is no separate wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: IVF, in vitro fertilisation, is conception in a laboratory dish, which gave rise to the term test-tube baby.

clue.text: Preferred dated number vocalised by Brenda?

indicators.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, and her clipped upper-class vowel turns the number into this sound

parts.note: five, a number, spoken in an old-fashioned upper-class accent

explanation.surface: The Queen sings her favourite golden oldie.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the Queen 'Brenda'; 'vocalised by Brenda' means five in her plummy accent, which sounds like 'fave'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fave is informal for favourite, the one most liked; the clue's word is used as an adjective.

clue.text: Randy type's one-piece — oo-er! captivates servile public schoolboy

parts.note: A means one
a bit is a piece

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the exclamation holds the schoolboy within it

parts.note: the exclamation spelt out as letters
at English public schools a fag was a junior boy who ran errands for a senior

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a sexy swimsuit, gasps, and so entrances a fawning schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: OOER 'captivates' FAG after its first O, giving OFAGOER, read as 'of a goer'. The 's of 'type's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a goer is a sexually eager person, so a bit of a goer is someone fairly randy.

clue.text: The president gets to shag Blair's no.2

parts.note: to have someone is crude slang for having sex with them
the second letter of Blair is L

explanation.surface: Gossip about a president seducing Tony Blair's deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair's number two looks like his deputy, John Prescott, but it is just the second letter of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Václav Havel was president of Czechoslovakia and then the Czech Republic around the time of this puzzle.

clue.text: Cuddly Australian bloke involved with AA meets a boozer's end

indicators.note: involved here means tangled up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: only the last letter is used

parts.note: its last letter is R

explanation.surface: An Australian man joins Alcoholics Anonymous and meets a drunkard's fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges BLOKE, AA and A into KOALABEA; 'end' of 'boozer's' adds R. 'Cuddly' belongs to the definition, not to the bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala bear is a furry Australian marsupial, often thought of as huggable, the model for cuddly toys.
